doc.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012

title: Finding titles; not programmatic music
summary: He keeps lists of titles; his titles have meaning but the music is not programmatic.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you ever have trouble finding titles?
All the time. And I keep lists of things that seem good. And that helps sometimes, and sometimes it’s pretty hysterical when you go back to that list and it’s like really? I

thought that was going to be a good title? But there’s a book that I have somewhere called All We Need is a Title. And it’s all about the working titles of famous books. And some of them were just awful, but it’s interesting to read just what people thought they were going to call something, and famous books, like Moby Dick — I can’t remember what the original like working title was but it was not that, and so it would have been a whole different experience.

Right, something like that. You know, and so, but, yeah, that’s always an issue. I’ve played dictionary roulette where I just opened and — I can’t really use that word — I mean everything to try and find —
Because titles can really spin the listener I think. I mean it’s like looking at an abstract painting — it’s better to look at it without seeing it, at least for me.

I have to look at it first without seeing what it’s called. But if I said, oh, “Beyond the Fall,” that must have some deep meaning, like I’m going to try to figure this out. Does any of your music have —
The titles have a meaning but the music itself does not necessarily. It’s not — what do you call that —
I’m trying to think of the word.
It’s not picturesque — that’s not the word, what is it called? AR: Programmatic?

Yes, thank you. It’s not programmatic. So I’ve never really written a piece like this is about my friend Jim, or whatever, like and his life and his struggles. Like it’s never been that. But the titles all have some significance. And once in a while the band gets me at the gig talking about and explaining the title.
